title: Delegated Tenant Shaper with Predictive Autoscaler and Graceful Spillback
creator: Aisha Malik
description:
Problem: Tenants on Dedicated fleets occasionally spike in demand and either breach latency SLOs or cause noisy-neighbor effects when autoscalers react slowly. We need a routing-layer mechanism that enforces tenant-level throughput contracts while allowing benign short bursts and providing graceful degradation paths when capacity is constrained.

Goal: Implement a Delegated Tenant Shaper (DTS) in the ingress router that combines: predictive scale hints from the Autoscaler Forecast service, an admission shaper that enforces soft throughput envelopes per-tenant, bounded local queueing with latency caps, and graceful spillback to lower-cost model variants or cross-region pools when appropriate. The system must be observable per-tenant and allow operators to tune burst budgets and demotion policies.

Design summary:
- Forecast-driven reservation: Autoscaler Forecast emits short-horizon demand forecasts (t+0..t+60s). DTS consumes forecasts to pre-allocate soft slot reservations for tenants (fastpath).
- Delegated admission: Instead of a centralized global gate, each router shard runs a lightweight delegating shaper that enforces per-tenant rate windows and burst tokens. The shaper can delegate temporary extra capacity if forecast suggests short bursts.
- Bounded slowpath queue: Requests that exceed immediate admission enter a local bounded queue (configurable per-tenant) with a strict per-request max-wait timeout (latency SLO contributor).
- Graceful spillback and demotion: When local queue and reservations saturate, DTS initiates multi-step fallbacks: 1) try compatible cheaper model variant in same fleet, 2) route to a dedicated low-priority pool, 3) return structured 429 with retry-after and suggested model/mode. Spillback policy is weighted by tenant SLA tier and historical error budget.
- Operator controls: UI knobs for per-tenant envelope, burst budget, demotion order, queue depth, and forecast confidence threshold.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Per-tenant throughput envelopes are enforced with <=2% SLA breach in steady-state bench tests.
2) Mean-99 latency for admitted requests remains within configured SLO during 3x synthetic spikes.
3) Spillback path triggers correctly and returns structured responses with routing hints.
4) End-to-end observability: dashboards show forecast vs actual, admission accepts/rejects, queue depth, spillback counts per-tenant.

Trade-offs considered:
- Centralized vs delegated: delegation reduces cross-shard coordination latency but adds risk of transient overcommit; we mitigate using conservative forecast-confidence scaling and small global reconciliation heartbeat.
- Hard guarantees vs soft envelopes: chosen soft envelopes allow graceful degradation without global throttles that can underutilize capacity.
- Complexity vs rollout speed: MVP ships without cross-region orchestration; cross-region demotion is planned for follow-up.

Security/Privacy: No tenant payload inspected; only metadata (tenant id, qps, estimated tokens) used. KMS notes: use existing control-plane auth for forecast stream.

Docs & artifacts: Design doc in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/DTS-Design, prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4876, bench scripts: https://ci.redwood.ai/jobs/dts-bench.
comments: 2026-02-16 - Kickoff: scoped MVP and tech spikes. Aisha created forecast consumer PoC and validated t+30s smoothing reduces false positives.
2026-02-23 - Spike update: Local shaper prototype (golang) shows median admission latency 0.6ms; queueing tail increases predictably at high load. Jonah will wire in forecast stream next.
2026-03-02 - Design review: PM & SRE feedback: (1) add structured 429 payload, (2) provide emergency global freeze signal for safety, (3) ensure metrics compatibility with console. Added to TODOs.
2026-03-07 - PR opened: infra#4876 implements shaper and forecast consumer. Early integration tests green for single-shard scenarios. Requesting code review from Riley Chen and Marco DiPasquale.

2026-03-10 - Integration bench: ran 3x synthetic tenant spike (10s bursts). Observed 95th queue wait 220ms, M99 latency for admitted 85ms (target 120ms). Spillback to low-priority pool occurred for 2 tenants as expected. Next: add structured 429 handling in SDKs and console alerting hooks.
